THE ACCEPTED-DIVERGENCE LEDGER FOR bc23, AND IT IS EMPTY.

Root-cause-or-fail is the standing rule and it is the operator's ruling on the bc26 run (Fleet card 1218171523823317), not a preference: an unexplained Tier C divergence is a FAIL, not a ledger line. Every entry would have to name a round, a map and a ROOT CAUSE, and tools/ci/parity_tiers_bc23.py rejects a cause of "unknown".

It is empty because it can be. MEASURED ON THIS TREE, in the sandbox, before the job was written: all six trace pairs -- examplefuncsplayer23 against itself on Quiet, SmallElements, Lantern, Spin, Sneaky and Barcode -- are BIT-EXACT FOR WHOLE 2000-ROUND GAMES, 96k to 270k trace lines a side, with the traced bytecode peak at 5-7 % of the limit (745-893 of the carrier's 12 500) and ZERO mid-turn cut-offs. That is a better shipped state than bc21's (22-245-round windows, five root-caused entries) or bc25's, and it is why this year's note could promise an empty ledger.

An entry here would look like:
  {"bot": "examplefuncsplayer23", "map": "Sneaky", "first_divergent_round": 1412, "cause": "one sentence naming the RULE that differs", "docs": "PARITY.md#bc23-anchor"}
